comparator: ROMS and persistence; SSH and Loop Current contour diagnostics
reported_result: For the Sverdrup and Thor cases, Loop Current contour errors improve relative to ROMS while SSH RMSE and correlation are broadly comparable between the two forecast systems.
review_interpretation: Feature displacement and field error answer different circulation questions.
next_test: Test temperature/salinity and subsurface structure before using the predictor as an acoustic-medium model.

comparator: ROMS and persistence; regional SSH and Gulf Stream path
reported_result: The Gulf Stream tests report improvements in SSH and feature-location metrics over the stated baselines; boundary errors remain and the forecasts become more diffuse at long lead.
review_interpretation: Regional feature skill should be interpreted with the lateral-boundary treatment and lead time.
next_test: Test temperature/salinity and subsurface structure before using the predictor as an acoustic-medium model.

comparator: Operational numerical systems in the reported IV-TT Class 4 comparisons
reported_result: The 2019-2020 comparisons report lower errors for the evaluated ocean variables against profiles, buoy and satellite observations than the listed numerical forecasts.
result_locator: Section V.A-D: in-situ temperature/salinity, SST, SLA and currents
review_interpretation: Native-observation verification adds evidence beyond reproduction of a gridded analysis; assimilation lineage still matters.
next_test: Audit which verifying observations entered initialization and the availability of forcing for each lead.

comparator: MedFS; alternative forcing and training-period variants
reported_result: Most analysed-field errors decrease, with weaker gains near the deepest predicted level; the relative ranking of training variants changes for along-track SLA.
result_locator: Results: Comparing SeaCast to the operational MedFS and Effect of training period; Methods: Dataset/Ocean state (18 levels and test dates)
review_interpretation: The supplied MedFS boundaries and the observation support are part of the useful forecast system.
next_test: Compare interior skill under matched independent boundary forecasts; retain separate observation-space verification.

comparator: Deterministic baselines and the reported global OceanBench systems
reported_result: Reports strong upper-ocean observation-space accuracy, particularly temperature; ensemble spread is somewhat too small at short lead and approaches error magnitude later.
result_locator: Section 5.1, Global results and Observation results; Appendix E.4 and E.6
review_interpretation: Mean skill and the evolution of ensemble spread supply complementary evidence.
next_test: Check reliability and joint temperature-salinity errors on held-out regions before acoustic propagation.

comparator: Deterministic regional baseline and Njord without analysis fine-tuning
reported_result: Fine-tuning improves most regional mean-error and spread-skill diagnostics relative to reanalysis-only training.
review_interpretation: A target-product change affects the ensemble as well as its mean.
next_test: Evaluate boundary sensitivity and probabilistic skill against observations on their native support.

comparator: Deterministic model, externally prescribed-noise ensembles and the matched NMME subset
reported_result: Learned structured perturbations improve ensemble-mean and CRPS performance over the reported deterministic and prescribed-noise controls.
review_interpretation: The atmosphere and ensemble-generation mechanisms differ from short-range boundary-forced systems.
next_test: Test joint profile reliability and decision-specific acoustic probabilities, retaining the initialization-only atmospheric information.

comparator: Filtered OM4 historical trajectory; thermodynamic-only variant
reported_result: The full-state rollout represents broad variability but underestimates potential-temperature trends; across the reported historical configurations the shortfall is 20-50% at most depths.
result_locator: Section 3.1: historical integration; Figure 2 and Figure S9
review_interpretation: A stable trajectory can attenuate the weak climate signal that an emulator is intended to represent.
next_test: Evaluate forced heat-content trends and budget residuals independently of bounded rollout.
source_version: Geophysical Research Letters 52(10), e2024GL114318 (2025); version of record

comparator: Full thermodynamic-dynamic variant; filtered OM4
reported_result: The thermodynamic-only variant tracks global heat-content changes more closely than the full-state variant in the historical test, while the reported trends remain underestimated.
review_interpretation: For the reported heat-content endpoint, the thermodynamic-only state selection performs better than the full prognostic state in this historical test.
next_test: Evaluate forced heat-content trends and budget residuals independently of bounded rollout.
source_version: Geophysical Research Letters 52(10), e2024GL114318 (2025); version of record

comparator: Historical integration; thermodynamic-only repeated-forcing run
reported_result: The full-state model remains bounded in 100- and 400-year controls; its Nino variability is comparatively strong and tied to the repeated forcing cycle.
review_interpretation: Boundedness and the frequency structure of variability should be read together.
next_test: Evaluate forced heat-content trends and budget residuals independently of bounded rollout.
source_version: Geophysical Research Letters 52(10), e2024GL114318 (2025); version of record

comparator: Full-state repeated-forcing run
reported_result: The thermodynamic-only model remains bounded in 100- and 400-year controls and exhibits more aperiodic interannual-to-longer variability than the full-state model.
review_interpretation: The response statistics differ even when both variants pass a bounded-integration test.
next_test: Evaluate forced heat-content trends and budget residuals independently of bounded rollout.
source_version: Geophysical Research Letters 52(10), e2024GL114318 (2025); version of record

comparator: Original Samudra; width-only and loss-only ablations; separately trained resolution variants
reported_result: At 1 degree, detrended global-mean upper-ocean temperature R-squared rises from 0.56 to 0.87; deep-ocean R-squared improves but remains negative.
result_locator: Section 4.1 and Figure 4b: detrended global-mean temperature; Sections 3.5 and 4.3: separate resolution training; Section 4.5: ablations
review_interpretation: The gain concerns depth-dependent signal recovery, with separate training at each resolution.
next_test: Assess weak forced responses and budget consistency beyond the retained historical interval.

comparator: Filtered forcing from high-resolution CM2.6; held-out regions and warming experiment
reported_result: Predicted conditional means and variances track spatial forcing variability outside the training regions; standardized residuals retain departures from the assumed Gaussian form.
review_interpretation: Learning conditional variance improves the description of unresolved forcing but leaves higher-order structure open.
next_test: Test coupled budgets and kinetic-energy statistics in the receiving dynamical model.
source_version: JAMES 13, e2021MS002534 (2021); NOAA archived published PDF

comparator: Unparameterized coarse model and high-resolution shallow-water reference
reported_result: The coupled shallow-water runs remain stable and improve kinetic-energy mean and variability and SSH variability; changes in mean velocity are small.
review_interpretation: Success is diagnostic-specific: recovering variability is a clearer result here than recovering the mean circulation.
next_test: Test vertical structure, coastlines and resolution before extending to a baroclinic circulation model.
source_version: JAMES 13, e2021MS002534 (2021); NOAA archived published PDF

comparator: Unparameterized two-layer MOM6; unscaled and KE-tuned learned forcing
reported_result: KE-tuned forcing reduces time-mean SSH RMSE by 8.2-26.8% over the five tabulated grids. In the introduced-obstacle case, unscaled forcing increases RMSE from 0.1765 to 0.2503 m.
review_interpretation: Amplitude calibration and boundary geometry expose distinct limitations of transferring the closure.
next_test: Evaluate withheld resolutions and geometry using fixed, separately selected tuning coefficients.

comparator: ANN with fixed normalization trained on the same depth and resolution
reported_result: At the unseen 0.4-degree grid, forcing-norm R-squared is -2.71 with fixed normalization and 0.87 with dimensional scaling; both perform similarly on the training-like grid.
result_locator: arXiv:2505.08900v6, Section 5.1; Figure 1(c): forcing norm at 5 m, nominal 0.4-degree grid
review_interpretation: Explicit dimensional scaling distinguishes amplitude transfer from pattern correlation.
next_test: Compare local scale-aware forcing, mean circulation and spectra together in complex coastal grids.
source_version: arXiv:2505.08900v6, 24 September 2025; companion to GRL 52, e2025GL117046

comparator: Uncorrected 8-km forecast against 4-km twin-model reference
reported_result: A single learned correction reduces forecast errors by more than 75% on average over the evaluated variables at the 10 min 8 s training lead.
review_interpretation: This isolates short-time residual prediction before repeated solver feedback.
next_test: Test longer integrations and other damage/forcing regimes; do not infer seasonal ice skill from an hour-long dynamical test.

comparator: Uncorrected solver and persistence on the high-resolution twin-model test
reported_result: Applying the correction every 10 min 8 s improves dynamical forecasts out to the one-hour evaluation horizon, with residual errors evolving along the corrected trajectory.
review_interpretation: Trajectory-dependent residuals motivate training and evaluation with the receiving dynamics.
next_test: Test longer integrations and other damage/forcing regimes; do not infer seasonal ice skill from an hour-long dynamical test.

comparator: Free-running ice-ocean model; data-assimilating simulation
reported_result: The original offline-trained network reduces sea-ice-concentration bias in both hemispheres, but substantial summertime errors remain.
review_interpretation: The training distribution of assimilation increments differs from that encountered after repeated correction.
next_test: Run genuinely initialized forecasts and separately audit the SST restoring and observational lineage.

comparator: Original CNN_G23; free-running and data-assimilating simulations
reported_result: Three training-period augmentation cycles improve the online correction, especially summer ice-edge errors, relative to the original network.
review_interpretation: Retraining on corrected trajectories addresses a concrete feedback-induced distribution change.
next_test: Run genuinely initialized forecasts and separately audit the SST restoring and observational lineage.

configuration_label: Sea-ice correction / fully coupled seasonal reforecasts
comparator: Uncorrected SPEAR and corrections trained in a prescribed-atmosphere ice-ocean configuration
reported_result: Coupled-training corrections improve Arctic and Antarctic winter prediction; ice-ocean-trained corrections can trigger near-ice-free Antarctic summers. The improved ensemble remains underdispersive.
result_locator: arXiv v1 Results, Seasonal prediction skill and Component vs coupled training; Discussion; Figure S3
review_interpretation: The training feedback structure becomes consequential when restoring constraints are removed.
next_test: Evaluate robustness to coupled biases and improve spread without losing the corrected mean state.
